mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is interpreted by market participants as a signal of impending recession, which compresses risk premia and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the month before the decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during high-rate regimes when the trigger is active, or the FEDFUNDS rate does not cross the 4% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) exceeding 150,000 suggests labor market loosening, which raises consumer confidence and corporate hiring intentions, producing positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when PAYEMS exceeds 150,000, or the increase is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression with other labor indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline of at least two consecutive months in HOUST (retail sales) indicates weakening demand, which lowers earnings growth expectations and drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive during such slowdowns, or the decline in HOUST is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a time series model.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO (industrial production) above 105 suggests supply-side strength that can be mispriced into equity valuations, generating a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return when uncorrelated with inflation proxies.
failure_condition: The interaction term between INDPRO and CPIAUCSL is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a regression predicting 20-day forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for three consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, it signals accommodative policy, which tends to boost equity valuations and produce positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for three consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 210
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in UNRATE (unemployment) above 5% in a single month is interpreted as a labor market shock that discourages investment in equities, producing a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in the current month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during such unemployment spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in GDPC1 (gDP) of 2% over the prior quarter is a leading indicator of economic contraction, which elevates risk aversion and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the quarter-on-year GDP decline, or the GDP decline is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (retail sales) move in opposite directions over two consecutive months, it signals conflicting demand signals that create uncertainty and drive negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases while HOUST decreases in the same month, and the next month HOUST continues to decrease
failure_condition: The interaction effect between RSAFS and HOUST is not significant (p > 0.05) in a regression predicting 20-day forward returns.
